title: Retire task time-cap presentation in VS Code
description: Objective: remove deprecated task time-budget presentation and client fields, after JetBrains retirement lands. Deliverable: task details and board cards ignore legacy time-budget data, while existing uncapped elapsed wall-clock and other live metrics remain. Scope exactly five files: moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts (remove task.budget, its visibility contribution, and remaining KPI from renderMetrics); moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts (remove TaskBudget and Task.budget); moe-vscode/media/board.js (replace budgetSuffix/cap ratios/indicators with the existing elapsed-only presentation); moe-vscode/src/providers/BoardViewProvider.ts (rename matching inline badge class/style); new moe-vscode/tests/task-time-budget.test.cjs. Test the actual TaskDetailPanel-generated HTML and actual media/board.js renderTaskCard with node:test, TypeScript transpileModule and node:vm, following tests/daemon-start.test.cjs; do not duplicate renderer logic or add a dependency. Stub required IDE/DOM/transport hooks, fail loudly for unexpected dependencies, and dispose clients/timers in finally. Compare output for identical tasks with/without legacy caps; missing/null/malformed legacy data must be ignored without throws. Preserve existing uncapped timing gates/fallbacks, HTML escaping, steps/reopens/rejects/wall-clock, critiques, failed DoD and handoffs. Do not introduce a new recorded-duration-only badge where current uncapped behavior omits it. NOT in scope: taskDetail.js, other media styles with no budget usage, live chat/reopen limits, daemon schema/deprecation/data rewriting, percentage metrics fix, or additional time-tracking features. Exact gate from repo root on Windows: npm --prefix moe-vscode test; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }; npm --prefix moe-vscode run compile; exit $LASTEXITCODE. Unix: npm --prefix moe-vscode test && npm --prefix moe-vscode run compile. Use npm.cmd if PowerShell policy blocks npm.ps1, and preserve foreign work.
definitionOfDone: TaskDetailPanel no longer reads task.budget or renders remaining/cap values; a budget-only task has no empty Metrics section.
The board's actual renderTaskCard output has no legacy cap denominator, utilization warning/approval indicators or task-budget class, and retains the existing elapsed-only output and HTML escaping.
TaskBudget and Task.budget are removed from the VS Code client model; valid live TaskMetrics durations and counters remain supported.

Native node:test regressions cover actual detail and board renderers with absent, populated, null and malformed legacy budget values plus timestamp edge cases; populated-cap assertions fail on old rendered output.
Steps, reopens, rejects, wall-clock fallback, critique/failed-DoD/handoff data and live chat/reopen limits remain unchanged.
Full moe-vscode npm test and npm run compile pass with positive test counts and captured red-first regression evidence.
taskRails: Keep the five-file scope; no runtime/test framework changes or taskDetail.js churn.
Preserve existing uncapped wall-clock behavior and error handling, rather than deleting useful elapsed timing along with the retired cap.
JetBrains prerequisites land first; do not weaken their tests.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Deleting the board badge function entirely - rejected: its uncapped branch is the presentation the Definition of Done says to retain, and deleting it would remove live elapsed-time display along with the retired cap, which a task rail forbids. Dropping the early return so every task with a recorded duration gets a badge - rejected for the same reason in reverse: that would introduce a badge where today none appears. Keeping the retired class name to avoid touching the provider - rejected: the name is part of the retired vocabulary and the Definition of Done asks for the rename; it is a one-line selector change with identical declarations. Writing the tests against a copy of the render logic - rejected by the task description and by the existing convention, which transpiles and executes the real source, and which is also what makes a genuine red possible before any change. Removing usedMs along with the cap KPI - rejected: the wall-clock KPI still needs it, and that mistake would silently delete a live metric.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured live on 2026-09-11. The decisive fact is that the uncapped presentation already exists: board.js budgetSuffix has two branches, and when no cap is present it already emits the elapsed-only label with a wall-clock tooltip and no status mark. So this retirement deletes a branch rather than designing new output, which is exactly why the task rails forbid inventing a new recorded-duration-only badge. The subtlety that decides correctness is the early return at line 814, `if (capMs == null && !firstClaimAt) return ''`: today a task with a recorded wallClockMs but no firstClaimAt and no cap renders nothing, and that must stay true after the cap disappears, so the guard becomes a firstClaimAt check rather than being dropped. The elapsed fallback that derives a duration from firstClaimAt to doneAt or to now, with its unparseable-timestamp guard, is live behavior in both the board and the detail panel and must survive. In TaskDetailPanel, usedMs has two consumers - the wall-clock KPI and the retired cap KPI - so only the second goes, and the budget term must also leave the empty-section guard, which is what makes a cap-only task stop rendering an empty Metrics heading. There are exactly six occurrences of the retired term across src and media, all inside the five owned files, and taskDetail.js has none, which is why the scope excludes it.
planningNotes.risks: The guard at board.js:814 is the likeliest defect: change it carelessly and either every task grows a badge it never had, or tasks that should show elapsed time lose it. Pin both directions with tests. Do not delete the elapsed derivation or its timestamp guards while removing the cap. In the detail panel, keep usedMs and remember the empty-section guard, or a cap-only task will still render a bare Metrics heading and the first Definition-of-Done item fails. After the class rename, the emitted markup and the inline style must still agree - they live in two different files. The red must be an assertion failure about differing rendered output, not a transpile error, or it proves nothing about the old behavior. These files are contended: task-c6e2eca5e19f4aaf9323f02aefadb29a edits the same types, board and detail panel and is sequenced behind this one, so land cleanly. Keep taskDetail.js untouched - it is explicitly out of scope. If the PowerShell execution policy blocks the npm shim, use npm.cmd rather than changing the gate command.
